title: Shortfall: invoice exception workbench
shortDescription: Resolve invoice quantity discrepancies with cited evidence, approvals tied to current records, and durable execution. Shortfall runs on Vultr and tracks a case from a late receipt through an approved supplier credit.
longDescription:
Shortfall helps accounts payable reviewers resolve invoices for goods their receiving team has not accepted. Each case combines source evidence, assigned follow-up work, a proposed internal ledger change, approval, and execution history.

The key behavior is approval validity when evidence changes. In the synthetic demonstration, an invoice bills 120 units at $40, while receiving records show 100. A late receipt adds ten units and changes the discrepancy from $800 to $400. Shortfall rejects the old approval. After the reviewer approves the revised hold and a verified $400 supplier credit, the worker reconciles the invoice to $4,400 while keeping ten purchase-order units open.

Vultr hosts the Next.js application, API, PostgreSQL database, and durable worker. Claude Opus 5.5 extracts fields and exact source quotes; code validates evidence, calculates money, checks current approval versions, and applies idempotent changes. The deployed workflow, restart recovery, backup restoration, and budget limits have been exercised.

The frozen 24-document evaluation accepted 9/12 supported documents exactly and sent three CSVs to review; all 12 challenge expectations passed. After a CSV validation correction, the three targeted reruns passed. A separate fresh four-CSV check accepted two supported documents and withheld two as expected. These small synthetic sets are reported separately.

The prototype supports independent cases, text-based documents, USD, whole units, and one invoice per supplier/purchase order. It uses synthetic data and an internal ledger, with no payments or ERP writes. The target buyer is a distributor's finance manager. Operator interviews, authenticated roles, and an accounting connector are next; customer demand and a proposed $99 monthly pilot price remain unvalidated.
